title: Cable-effect pullover
excerpt: A drop-shoulder pullover in aran yarn with an all-over cable-effect pattern made by crossing fpdc columns in pairs. The cables run vertically up the front and back. Graded XS to 3XL.
sourceNotes: Cable-effect crochet pullovers using fpdc crossover technique are a popular intermediate garment project.

glossaryTerms.definition: A cable effect made by skipping the next fpdc post and working an fpdc around the post two stitches ahead, then going back to work an fpdc around the skipped post. The two posts cross on the fabric surface to mimic a knitted cable twist.
A dc worked around the post from behind. In the cable pattern, bpdc columns separate the fpdc cables and recede into the background to let the cables stand out.

crochet.gaugeText: 14 dc x 16 rows = 10 x 10 cm in aran on a 5 mm hook.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Graded XS to 3XL. Size M: 104.3 cm bust.

content.text: pattern across the body: work pairs of fpdc cables every 6 stitches, separated by pairs of
. On the cable row (every 6 rows), skip the first fpdc and work fpdc around the second, then fpdc around the first to cross. Work bpdc over bpdc throughout.
Size M: 146 sts wide, 81.7 cm body. Sleeve 63.3 cm.
Chain 148. Establish cable repeat on row 1. Cable-cross every 6th row. Work for 81.7 cm. Shape neck. Seam shoulders.
Chain 56. Work cable repeat, increasing each end every 4 rows for 63.3 cm.
The cable-effect open cardigan uses the same cable repeat opened down the centre front.
